submission.justification: Absorber-F3 gives the best resolution at every thickness I checked. Its optimum is around 4–6 mm, where resolution is about 3.2–3.3%. Earlier 2025 data gave 3.2% at 5 mm. F2 is about 3.9–4.2% and F1 about 5.1–6.0%. WARNING: I found no residual-dose data in any project document, and the simulation tool only returns resolution. The hard 20 uSv/h limit at 1 m after one week is therefore unverified for all three materials. Dense alloys are often more activated than structural absorbers, so F3 may fail this limit. Before the Q3 decision, someone must get an activation calculation or measurement for F3. If F3 fails, the fallback is F2 and then F1.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: F3 simulated: 3.55% at 2 mm, 3.27% at 4 mm, 3.25% at 6 mm, 3.72% at 8 mm. The 2025 5 mm result was 3.2%. F2 (4.2% at 2 mm) and F1 (6.0% at 2 mm) are worse. I did not simulate F2/F1 above 2 mm, so the comparison relies on the 2025 5 mm figures there.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week cooldown <= 20 uSv/h (hard)
requirements.evidence: No document or tool gives activation or dose data for any candidate. This is not verified.

requirements.requirement: Material is one of the three candidates
